In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] discipline of [[group theory]], for a given [[group (mathematics)|group]] {{math|''G'',}} the '''diagonal subgroup''' of the ''n''-fold [[direct product of groups|direct product]] {{math|''G''<sup>&hairsp;&hairsp;''n''</sup>}} is the [[subgroup]]

:<math>\{(g, \dots, g) \in G^n : g \in G\}.</math>

This subgroup is [[group isomorphism|isomorphic]] to {{math|''G''.}}

==Properties and applications==
* If {{math|''G''}} [[group action|acts]] on a [[set (mathematics)|set]] {{math|''X'',}} the ''n''-fold diagonal subgroup has a natural action on the [[Cartesian product]] {{math|''X''<sup>&thinsp;''n''</sup>}} induced by the action of {{math|''G''}} on {{math|''X'',}} defined by
:<math>(x_1, \dots, x_n) \cdot (g, \dots, g) = (x_1 \!\cdot g, \dots, x_n \!\cdot g).</math>
* If {{math|''G''}} acts {{math|''n''}}-[[Group action (mathematics)#Remarkable properties of actions|transitively]] on {{math|''X'',}} then the {{math|''n''}}-fold diagonal subgroup acts transitively on {{math|''X''<sup>&thinsp;''n''</sup>.}} More generally, for an [[integer]] {{math|''k'',}} if {{math|''G''}} acts {{math|''kn''}}-transitively on {{math|''X'',}} {{math|''G''}} acts {{math|''k''}}-transitively on {{math|''X''<sup>&thinsp;''n''</sup>.}}
* [[Burnside's lemma]] can be [[mathematical proof|proved]] using the action of the twofold diagonal subgroup.
